facts: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.
The country's highest point was renamed Mount Obama in 2009 and reverted to Boggy Peak in name only locally.
Nelson's Dockyard is the only continuously working Georgian-era naval dockyard in the world.
The Bahamas is an archipelago of around 700 islands and cays, about 30 of them inhabited.
Dean's Blue Hole off Long Island is one of the deepest known underwater sinkholes.
It is one of the few countries whose highest point is under 100 metres.
Barbados is made largely of coral limestone rather than volcanic rock, unlike most of its neighbours.
It became a republic in 2021, replacing the British monarch with a president.
Rum distilling began here in the 17th century, and Mount Gay claims to be the oldest surviving brand.
Belize is the only country in Central America where English is the official language.
The Belize Barrier Reef is the second largest reef system in the world after Australia's.
The capital moved inland to Belmopan in 1970 after a hurricane devastated Belize City.
Canada has the longest coastline of any country, at over 200,000 kilometres.
It contains more lake area than the rest of the world combined.
Its border with the United States is the longest international land border anywhere.
Costa Rica abolished its army in 1949 and has not reinstated one.
Around a quarter of its land is protected, and it holds roughly 5% of the world's biodiversity.
It has run for long stretches on almost entirely renewable electricity.
Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean, bigger than all the others combined by land area.
It has one of the highest doctor-to-population ratios in the world and exports medical staff abroad.
Old Havana preserves one of the largest collections of Spanish colonial architecture in the Americas.
Dominica is known as the Nature Island for its rainforest and volcanic terrain.
Boiling Lake is the second largest hot lake in the world, kept simmering by volcanic activity.
It has the last remaining pre-Columbian Kalinago community in the eastern Caribbean.
The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
Pico Duarte is the highest peak in the entire Caribbean.
Santo Domingo was the first permanent European settlement in the Americas, founded in 1496.
El Salvador is the smallest and most densely populated country on the Central American mainland.
It is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coastline.
In 2021 it became the first country to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender.
Grenada is called the Spice Isle and is a leading producer of nutmeg and mace.
Nutmeg appears on its national flag, the only flag to feature a spice.
Its capital, St. George's, is built around a submerged volcanic crater forming the harbour.
Volcán Tajumulco is the highest point in the whole of Central America, and one of more than thirty volcanoes running down the country's Pacific side.
Guatemala has the largest indigenous population share in Central America, with over twenty Mayan languages spoken.
Tikal, in the northern rainforest, was one of the most powerful cities of the Maya world.
Haiti became the first independent nation in Latin America and the first republic founded by former slaves, in 1804.
It shares Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic and occupies the western third.
The Citadelle Laferrière, built after independence to repel a French return, is the largest fortress in the Americas.
Copán holds some of the finest Maya sculpture and hieroglyphic inscriptions known.
Honduras has the second largest section of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, off its Bay Islands.
The Mosquitia rainforest in the east is one of the largest wilderness areas in Central America.
Jamaica is the birthplace of ska, rocksteady, reggae and dancehall, an unusual concentration of globally influential music for a country of under three million people.
Blue Mountain coffee, grown at high altitude, is among the most expensive in the world.
It has produced a remarkable number of world-record sprinters for a country of under three million people.
Mexico City is built on the drained bed of Lake Texcoco and is sinking by several centimetres a year.
Mexico is the world's largest producer of silver, and has been a major source of it since the Spanish colonial period.
Alongside Spanish it recognises 68 indigenous languages, spoken by several million people between them.
Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America by area.
Lake Nicaragua is the biggest lake in Central America and holds freshwater sharks and sawfish.
Ometepe island in the lake is formed by two volcanoes joined by an isthmus.
The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific across 82 kilometres and carries a large share of world shipping.
Because of the isthmus's curve, the sun rises over the Pacific and sets over the Atlantic in Panama City.
The Darién Gap is the only break in the Pan-American Highway, an impassable stretch of rainforest and swamp.
Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both area and population.
The two islands are separated by a strait about three kilometres wide.
Brimstone Hill Fortress is one of the best-preserved historic fortifications in the Americas.
The Pitons, two volcanic spires rising straight from the sea, are the island's defining landmark.
Saint Lucia changed hands between Britain and France fourteen times.
It has produced two Nobel laureates, giving it one of the highest rates per capita in the world.
The country comprises the main island of Saint Vincent plus a chain of smaller Grenadines.
La Soufrière is an active volcano that erupted significantly in 1902 and again in 2021.
The Tobago Cays are a group of uninhabited islands inside a horseshoe reef.
Trinidad sits on the South American continental shelf and was joined to the mainland during the last ice age.
The Pitch Lake is the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world.
The steelpan, developed in Trinidad in the 20th century, is one of the few acoustic instruments invented in modern times.
The United States spans six time zones across its states and territories, from Guam to Puerto Rico.
It has no official language at federal level, though English is used for government business.
Alaska alone would be the seventh largest country in the world if it were independent.
